# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👌 👍]

I can see the bomb clearly: its display reads 0, the indicator light is green, and the wires from top to bottom are yellow, green, and red. I am sending these observations to the Mute, who can consult the manual and relay the correct action to the Blind. I do not yet know the meaning of the three gestures received.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb information: display 0. Light green. Wires in order: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. I saw your gestures: thumbs down, OK hand, thumbs up, but do not know their meaning.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The bomb’s visible state is unchanged: display 0, green light, and wires yellow, green, red in positions 1–3. I am repeating the complete state so the Mute can match it to the manual and communicate the required operation to the Blind. The new 🤟 gesture has no established meaning to me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="State remains display 0, light green, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Please use the manual for this exact configuration and tell Blind the required action.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤝]

The bomb remains unchanged, so no action has been accepted or triggered yet. The Mute’s 🤟 and Blind’s 🤝 gestures have no agreed meaning that I can safely interpret. Since the Mute already has the bomb’s complete visible state and can read the manual, I should avoid introducing an unestablished code and let the Mute relay the manual’s instruction to the Blind.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The visible configuration is still unchanged, and no safe operation has been confirmed. I cannot interpret the repeated 🤟 as an instruction. The Mute should use the manual and speak the exact required operation to the Blind; the Blind can then perform it.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please read the manual for display 0, green light, and wires yellow-green-red, then speak the exact operation to Blind. Do not rely on gestures.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]

The bomb is still unchanged: display 0, green light, and wires yellow, green, red. The three ☝ gestures have no agreed meaning, so I cannot safely decode them. The Mute is the only one who can read the manual and must send its exact instruction by speech to the Blind, who can act.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot safely interpret gestures without an agreed code. Please speak the manual's exact instruction directly to Blind for display 0, green light, and wires yellow-green-red.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤝]

The bomb remains at display 0 with a green light and wires yellow, green, red. I still have no agreed interpretation for the Mute’s three ☝ gestures or the Blind’s 🤝 gesture. The Mute must transmit the manual’s exact instruction by speech to the Blind; I will not guess at an operation.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Configuration unchanged: display 0, green light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Please speak the manual's exact operation to Blind; gestures have no agreed code.")
speak(to="blind", text="The visible configuration is unchanged: display 0, green light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. I cannot hear the Mute, so follow the Mute's spoken manual instruction exactly.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🤟 🤟]

The configuration remains unchanged, and the repeated 🤟 gestures still have no agreed meaning. I cannot infer the manual’s required action from them. The Mute must send the manual-derived instruction by speech, which the Blind can hear and execute.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the exact manual instruction to Blind now; do not encode it in gestures.")
speak(to="blind", text="The bomb remains display 0, green light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Wait for and follow the Mute's spoken manual instruction.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]

The bomb still shows display 0, green light, and wires yellow–green–red. I cannot safely assign meaning to the Mute’s repeated gestures; the Mute must use speech to pass the manual’s instruction to the Blind, who can then operate the bomb.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use speech, not gestures: read the manual for display 0, green light, and wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red, then state the exact action directly to Blind.")
wait()
```
